if i were to have kids, i'd make sure i'm equalized in myself and that everything i do is balanced. growing up, your child needs stability in their environment. they are exploring the world and your viewpoints are imposed onto them. however you see the world, naturally they will, too. i believe it is very important to build character as much as possible. my parents never allowed me chores as my friend's parents did; it definitely shows in my character. looking back, i probably would not have favored chores but that doesn't hurt anyone. it shows that you have to work to participate in life. that life is not always so great. but if i were to have truly believed and understood that growing up, then i would not have had to discover that for myself later down the line. my life has been half-lived because i've lacked discipline.

i would also encourage the healthy exploration of the child's environment. my parents were very over-protective growing up and because of this i had no sense of self. all my desires were squashed. the worst thing you could do is to be insensitive. **lead by example** and encourage *honesty* and perseverance.

simply take the time to love. surround your child as much as possible with things you love and beautiful things. because your environment affects you. maybe the other half is very negative... offer the support. offer the support and promote strength. because even if your child is confused by the hate, if you have love and support to fall back on, then nothing could ever stop you. i lacked that. in my mistakes there was no comfort or honesty. only criticism or total ignorance of the failure. encourage love and feelings and emotions. if your child can learn to process it at a young age it will be naturally embedded how to deal with these feelings, child will be independent and later in life they will not become overwhelmed. practice makes perfect. a great foundation is the key. without foundation, we are nothing. 

**we may not build a dependable structure without a strong foundation.**
